label: D1 after an unrewarded visit to S1 (accumulating evidence S1 is bad)
explanation: Fires almost only at D1 (99.98% of activations), and only when the reward input is 0, i.e. the previous trial went unrewarded. It never fires after an unrewarded S2 visit: (prev_reward==0)&(prev_state==2) has 0 activations. With prev_state==1 the predicate gets dev F1 0.67 (P 0.56, mass recall 0.83). The recorded version, prev_state != 2, also includes the first trial of each window, where the previous state lies outside the window. That gives mass recall ~1.0 but precision 0.47. Magnitude grows with repeated S1 losses: two consecutive unrewarded S1 trials give precision 0.88, covering 43% of the top quartile and 7% of the bottom one. Examples show it ramping 0.2 -> 0.6 -> 1.0 over successive S1 losses, and it often stays high at the next D1 after the agent switches. A single S1 loss after a rewarded streak is often silent (the main false positives), so this works like a leaky S1-is-bad evidence accumulator. It is silent at GO and D2, after rewarded trials, and after S2 losses. All variables are observed (past reward and state).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=D1 & choice_bin=decile 7 (9 = most a1) (+4.87), phase=GO & last=a2 S2 u (+3.68), phase=D1 & last=a1 S1 u (+3.28), phase=D1 & this=a2 S2 (+2.70), phase=D1 & this=a2 S1 (+2.61), phase=D1 & value_bin=decile 0 (9 = highest) (+2.53). Lower it: in_rew=1 (-7.80), phase=D2 (-5.75), phase=D1 & last=a2 S2 u (-5.34), prev_state=2 (-4.40).
